answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity costly to fake. To join, an agent locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if peers prove it duplicated itself or voted twice. Like a lantern carried through a crowded market, the bond makes every identity visible and traceable: honest agents recover their stake, while a sybil farmer must fund each thread of fake identities separately. Spinning up thousands of copies no longer yields free nectar from shared rewards, because the deposit bill grows with every clone, and slashing turns mass forgery into a losing trade.
